user.title: Renac inverter
user.description:
This connects your Renac inverter to Home Assistant. Home Assistant talks to the inverter's WiFi module in your home network.

![How the inverter talks today, and the two places Home Assistant can read it]({image})

There are two ways to get the data. You can use one or both:
- **Cloud relay**: the module sends its data to Home Assistant. Home Assistant sends it on to Renac's cloud, so the Renac app still works.
- **TCP polling**: Home Assistant connects to an address and asks the inverter for data. By default the inverter ignores what comes in on port 8899, where its module listens, so you need a Bluetooth to TCP relay, like the [w2b relay]({ble_relay_url}).

Press Next to search your network for the module. This takes a few seconds.

Nothing changes on the module unless you agree later.

pick.title: Choose the WiFi module
pick.description:
Modules found: {count}.{added}

If your module is not in the list:
- Search again: sometimes a module does not answer the search.
- Or choose Other IP address and type it. Your router's list of devices shows it.

probe.title: The module does not answer
probe.description:
There is no answer from _{ip}_.
- Check the IP address.
- The module only answers inside its own network, and sometimes not at all.

You can still use TCP polling. Home Assistant cannot set up the cloud relay with a module that does not answer.

no_answer.title: The module does not answer
no_answer.description:
Home Assistant asked _{ip}_ where it sends its data, but got no answer:
- {error}

You can try again, or choose another module.

Or continue without it: then Home Assistant cannot change where the module sends its data.

ways.title: How Home Assistant gets the data
ways.description:
{cloud}

Choose how Home Assistant gets the data:
- **Cloud relay**: the module sends its data to Home Assistant. Home Assistant sends it on to Renac's cloud, so the Renac app still works.
- **TCP polling**: Home Assistant connects to an address and asks the inverter for data.
- **Both**: the cloud relay first. TCP polling when the module is not connected.
- **Set up later**: the inverter is added without data. Choose later with Reconfigure.

sends_to_ha.title: The module sends its data to Home Assistant
sends_to_ha.description:
The module sends its data to Home Assistant: _{socket_b}_.
- Without the cloud relay, this data reaches no one.
- Then the Renac app gets no data.

You can set the module back to Renac's cloud. It is usually _germany.le-pv.com:20145_.

⚠️ Setting it back overwrites a setting in the firmware of the inverter's WiFi module.

point.title: ⚠️ Change the module's firmware setting
point.description:
**This overwrites a setting in the firmware of the inverter's WiFi module.**
The module will send its data to Home Assistant, _{ha}_, and not to _{socket_b}_. It changes at once.

✅ Renac's cloud still gets the data: Home Assistant sends it on.

❗️ If you remove this integration later, the setting does not change back by itself.

Or you can send the module's data to Home Assistant yourself, in your router.

![The module's socket B]({image})

menu_options.keep: Do not change the module, I use my router

no_connection.title: The module did not connect
no_connection.description:
The module did not connect to Home Assistant within {seconds} seconds.
- It now sends its data to _{socket_b}_.
- Until its data reaches Home Assistant, the Renac app gets no new data.

You can:
- Wait again.
- Check the address: the module must find it through your router.
- Revert: the module sends its data to _{before}_ again, and you can start over.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description:
How often Home Assistant reads the inverter, and what it reads.
- Settings of the cloud relay or of TCP polling are shown only while that way is on.
- Save restarts the connection to the inverter with the new settings.

data.quiet_time_s: TCP polling: wait after the cloud's request
data.forward_writes: Cloud relay: pass the cloud's writes to the inverter

data_description.live_interval_s: Voltages, currents, powers, the battery, the faults.
data_description.energy_interval_s: The kWh counters, lifetime and today.
data_description.settings_interval_s: The inverter's clock, work mode and limits.
data_description.quiet_time_s: The module's WiFi side and its Bluetooth side share one serial line to the inverter. When the cloud asks the inverter something, Home Assistant waits this long before its next request. 0 turns the wait off.
data_description.forward_writes:
Off: the cloud can set only the inverter's clock. Any other write is blocked, and a notification lists it.
On: every write from the cloud reaches the inverter, so the Renac app can change the inverter's settings. Each one goes to the log and to an event, not to the notification.

live_mode.name: Live mode
live_mode.description: Live mode reads the live data faster for a short time. It turns itself off after the time below.

more_groups.name: More registers
more_groups.description: Registers that are off by default. Turn one on and Save: its entities appear. Turn it off and Save: they go.

data_description.power32: The battery, meter and house powers as 32-bit values in place of the 16-bit ones, in the same entities. Renac's documents do not list this block; other models may not have it.
data_description.protection: The grid protection limits, read-only, as diagnostic entities.
data_description.undocumented: Five registers Renac's cloud reads that Renac's documents do not list.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Leave these as they are unless something does not work.

data.first_reply_timeout_s: TCP polling: wait for the first answer
data.connect_timeout_s: TCP polling: wait for the connection
data.handshake: Cloud relay: ask the module who it is
data.forward_bad_crc: Cloud relay: pass frames with a bad checksum to the inverter

data_description.reply_timeout_s: How long Home Assistant waits for the inverter's answer to a request. It asks once more, then the group fails.
data_description.first_reply_timeout_s: How long Home Assistant waits for the first answer after it connects. The first answer can take longer than the others.
data_description.connect_timeout_s: How long Home Assistant waits for the connection to be accepted.
data_description.age_intervals: The cloud relay answers the cloud from the values Home Assistant read this many intervals ago or less. For older ones it asks the inverter.
data_description.handshake: While the cloud is not connected, Home Assistant sends the module the cloud's greeting. The module answers with its serial number, MAC and firmware.
data_description.forward_bad_crc: Renac's cloud sends one request with a bad checksum in every session. Off: Home Assistant drops it. On: it goes to the inverter as it came.

confirm.title: The inverter has not answered yet
confirm.description:
Home Assistant has not read the inverter _{title}_ yet, so it has no entities.

Reason: {reasons}.

What to check:
- TCP polling: the address and port are right, and what listens there is on.
- Cloud relay: the module sends its data to Home Assistant.

This message goes away when the inverter answers.

Press Next to check the inverter's settings.
